entries.title: API Client Enhancements
body: Authentication Service includes the following enhancements:
# Support for Authorization Code Flow
API clients now support the OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code flow and grant type, enabling applications to securely access Zscaler APIs on behalf of authenticated admins. This enhancement includes:
- Support for Client Identity Metadata Documents (CIMD) for client registration
- Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)
- User consent-based authorization with role-based access control (RBAC)
- Refresh tokens with rotation during refresh grant
- Ability to configure authorization grant duration
- OAuth authorization server metadata discovery through the .well-known endpoint to simplify client integration
- Centralized management of authorization grants, including the ability to view and revoke active grants
See image.
The existing Client Credentials grant type remains supported. An API client can be configured to use either the Authorization Code or Client Credentials grant type.
# Support for AI Agents
You can now configure and manage AI agents that access Zscaler APIs on behalf of authenticated administrators. This enhancement includes:
- Predefined AI client configurations for Claude Code and ChatGPT
- User consent-based authorization with role-based access control (RBAC)
- Audit logging for client management and authorization activities
See image.
To learn more, see About API and AI Agents, Adding an API or AI Agent, and About Authorization Grants.

entries.title: Enhancements to Authentication Service Pages
body: The Authentication Service pages in the Zscaler Admin Console are updated. The pages are intuitive and visually appealing to improve usability, navigation, and overall user experience.
To learn more, see What is Authentication Service?

entries.title: Support for Source IP Addresses and CIDR Ranges in API Client Access Policy
body: The OneAPI API client access policy framework is extended to support source IP addresses and Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) ranges as policy criteria. Administrators can select pre-configured trusted IP locations or trusted IP location groups as criteria while configuring the API client access policy rule to restrict specific OneAPI API clients and only accept API requests that originate from approved source IP addresses or CIDR ranges. OneAPI enforces the policy when an assigned API client invokes a Zscaler API.
See image.
To learn more, see About the API Client Access Policy and Adding API Client Access Policy Rule.

entries.title: Access Multiple Experience Center Tenants
body: Admins can now launch Experience Center tenants for multiple customers from the Partner Portal without logging out from the previously accessed tenant. Experience Center automatically opens the next tenant and maintains only one active browser session for all the accessed tenants.
To learn more, see About Tenants in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

entries.title: Access to Legacy Admin Portals Deprecated
body: Access to the following Zscaler service Admin Portals is deprecated:
- Internet Access (ZIA)
- Private Access (ZPA)
- Zscaler Client Connector
- Authentication Service
- Data Security and Posture Management (DSPM)
- Risk360
- Zscaler Cellular
- Workflow Automation
- Cloud & Branch Connector
- Digital Experience (ZDX)
- Zero Trust Branch
The corresponding legacy Admin Portals tiles are no longer displayed on the Authentication Service single sign-on (SSO) page. Use Experience Center to access these services.

entries.title: Unified Role-Based Access Control for Authentication Service
body: Authentication Service supports Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Administrators can now view, create, and manage Authentication Service roles centrally on the Role Management page (Administration > Role Management).
See image.
The existing options to configure roles, permissions, and administrative entitlements in Authentication Service are deprecated if you use Unified RBAC.
To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To learn more, see:
- About Role Management
- About Authentication Service Admin Roles
- Adding Authentication Service Admin Roles
- About Administrative Entitlements

entries.title: Customize Password Policy
body: You can now configure the password policy to deactivate a user account after a specific number of unsuccessful authentication attempts, and reject a specific number of previously used passwords. You can customize both values from 3 to 10 in the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Password Policy.

entries.title: Support for Creating Tenants in India Region
body: Authentication Service now provides support for creating tenants in the India region, in addition to the United States and European Union. To enable connectivity with Authentication Service, make sure to allowlist the required IP ranges in your environment.
To learn more, see Authentication Service Logs.

entries.title: Zscaler Cellular Portal Tile Removed from Authentication Service SSO Page
body: The Zscaler Cellular Portal tile is removed from the Authentication Service single sign-on (SSO) page. You can access Zscaler Cellular from Experience Center.
To learn more, see What is Zscaler Cellular?

entries.title: Support for End User Migration
body: Authentication Service is the global and centralized identity management platform for all the Zscaler products. You can now migrate all the users from your external IdPs to Authentication Service. This streamlines the identity management process and eliminates the need to configure the IdP for each Zscaler product separately, and instead manage all the idenitites within Authentication Service. After the migration, end users can authenticate with Authentication Service and access the assigned Zscaler services.
To learn more, see Migrating End Users to Authentication Service.

entries.title: Support for NSS Integration with Authentication Service
body: You can now integrate Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) and Cloud NSS with Authentication Service to stream Authentication Service logs to external security information and event management (SIEM) systems. You can store and monitor the Authentication Service admin audit, authentication, and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) logs.
See image.
To learn more, see About Log Streaming.

entries.title: Support for Integrating Two Private Access Tenants
body: Authentication Service provides support for integrating two Private Access (ZPA) tenants at a time. This allows customers to manage multiple tenants through the Zscaler Admin Console. The following authentication scenarios are supported for Private Access tenants:
For admins:
- Identity provider (IdP)-initiated single-sign on (SSO) to access all tenants from Authentication Service.
- Service provider-initiated SSO for all tenants.
- Access tenants by logging in to the Zscaler Admin Console.
For users:
- Zscaler Client Connector enrollment for Private Access tenants.
- Browser access for Private Access.
To learn more, see Customizing Your Account Settings and Multiple Private Access Tenant Support with Authentication Service.

entries.title: Authentication Service for End Users
body: For new deployments, Authentication Service now provides support for end users. Admins can manage a single identity for end users across all Zscaler services. End users have an improved user experience, as Zscaler Client Connector enrollment is faster, and they can securely log in once and access any of the assigned Zscaler services.
Authentication Service for end users centralizes user identity administration and enables new adaptive access use cases with Step-Up Authentication and the Adaptive Access Engine.
End user support for existing customers is coming soon.
To learn more, see What is Authentication Service?

entries.title: NSS Integration with Authentication Service
body: You can now integrate Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) and Cloud NSS with Authentication Service to stream Authentication Service logs to external security information and event management (SIEM) systems. You can store and monitor the Authentication Service admin audit, authentication, and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) logs.
To enable the Log Streaming feature, contact Zscaler Support.
See image.
To learn more, see About Log Streaming.

entries.title: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Authentication for SCIM Provisioning
body: Authentication Service provides support to use OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials for authentication while configuring SCIM provisioning with external identity providers (IdPs).
See image.

entries.title: Integration of Management Portal for Partners with Authentication Service
body: The Zscaler Management Portal for Partners is now integrated with Authentication Service. You can enable single sign-on (SSO) for partner logins and provide a unified authentication experience. You can assign roles and scopes to partner users migrated to Authentication Service from the Administrative Entitlements page.
See image.
To learn more, see Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups.

entries.title: Common Domain for Multiple Authentication Service Tenants
body: Authentication Service provides support for using the same domain for multiple tenants within a single Authentication Service cloud environment. If two or more tenants share a common domain, users might be prompted to select their tenant from a drop-down menu during login. This experience is applicable to the following services using OpenID Connect (OIDC) flow to redirect users to Authentication Service:
- Experience Center
- Zscaler Breach Predictor
- External Attack Surface Management (EASM)
- Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
See image.

entries.title: Enhancements to External Identities Certificate Management
body: The External Identities Certificate Management feature is updated with the following enhancements:
# Notification for SAML Certificate Expiration

If any of the SAML certificates (IdP Certificate or SAML Request Signing and Decryption Certificate) are about to expire within 90 days or have already expired, a banner appears on all the pages in the Authentication Service Admin Portal, and a visual indicator is displayed on the External Identities page. During the last 90 days before certificate expiration, the administrator receives weekly email reminders until the certificate is updated. After the certificate expires, the administrator receives two more reminder emails to take the necessary action.
See image.
To learn more, see About External Identity Providers.
# Upload Multiple IdP Certificates
Authentication Service provides support for uploading multiple IdP certificates, enabling seamless transition with IdP certificate rotations.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SAML Authentication Service Providers.
# Update SAML Request Signing and Decryption Certificate

You can add a new SAML Request Signing and Decryption Certificate when the existing one is about to expire or as needed. Administrators can select a new certificate before the old certificate expires to prevent authentication issues with the IdP.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding SAML Authentication Service Providers.

entries.title: Token Validators
body: You can create and use token validators in the Authentication Service Admin Portal to validate the JSON Web Token (JWT) that is used for authorization to access Zscaler services, like Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA).
See image.
To learn more, see About Token Validators, Adding a Token Validator, and Testing an Access Token.

entries.title: API Client Access Policy
body: You can now define API client access policy rules to manage the API client's access to specific resources within a set time frame. Administrators can define the policy rules and assign them to the required API clients. This allows you to control and manage authorization.
See image.
To learn more, see About the API Client Access Policy and Adding API Client Access Policy Rule.

entries.title: Updates to MFA
body: The SMS OTP authentication steps are updated and simplified. After entering the login ID and password, admins are no longer prompted to re-enter the country and phone number but can directly enter the SMS OTP for authentication.
To learn more, see Setting Up Your Zscaler Account and Configuring MFA.

entries.title: Authentication Events in Audit Logs
body: Administrators can view authentication login and logout events on the Audit Logs page. This provides visibility into the user authentication activities within your tenant.
See image.
To learn more, see About Audit Logs.

entries.title: APIs for Identity and Lifecycle Management
body: Authentication Service supports APIs that give you programmatic access for managing identity and authentication-related features. The APIs allow you to integrate with ZIdentity for seamless identity lifecycle management and API client management.
To access and use the APIs, you must add an API client. Only admins with full access to the API Clients & Resource role can add API clients.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Authentication Service APIs and Working with Authentication Service APIs.

entries.title: MFA for Admins Using External IdP
body: In Authentication Service, MFA is enabled for all new and existing identity providers (IdPs) by default. Admins authenticating through external IdPs have a 7-day grace period option to temporarily skip MFA. After the grace period, they are required to configure second-factor authentication in Authentication Service if the Enforce Zscaler Admin MFA option is enabled on either the Add Primary or Secondary Identity Provider page.

Admins using MFA through their external IdP can disable the Enforce Zscaler Admin MFA option to prevent additional authentication verification from Authentication Service. This allows admins to decide whether MFA is managed by Authentication Service, their external IdP, or both.
See image.
To learn more, see About External Identity Providers and Adding OpenID Providers.

entries.title: IdP-Initiated SSO Redirect
body: For new Authentication Service tenants enabled with Experience Center, the IdP-initiated SSO redirects users to Experience Center by default.
To learn more, see About External Identity Providers.

entries.title: Regenerate Registration Link
body: You can regenerate the one-time registration link if it becomes invalid after 72 hours. An email with a new registration link is sent to the registered email address, and this link remains valid for 24 hours. You can regenerate the registration link up to three times. After three attempts, contact Zscaler Support to request a new registration link.
See image.
To learn more, see Setting Up Your Zscaler Account.

entries.title: MFA Grace Period Removed
body: All Authentication Service admins are required to enroll for multi-factor authentication (MFA). The option to skip MFA enrollment for a default grace period of 14 days is no longer available. While authenticating to the subscribed Zscaler service admin portal for the first time, admins need to enroll for MFA immediately before accessing the Zscaler service admin portal.
To learn more, see Migrating Zscaler Service Admins to Authentication Service and Configuring Authentication Methods.

entries.title: Step-Up Authentication
body: Authentication Service supports step-up authentication over OpenID Connect protocol with external identity providers (IdP). You can define authentication levels and configure Zscaler policies to mandate user authentication at a particular level before allowing them to access sensitive resources.

Step-up authentication enhances security by mandating multi-factor authentication (MFA) when users attempt to access sensitive resources or when risk signals indicate potential threats. This feature allows organizations to configure hierarchical authentication levels, ensuring that access control is customized to resource sensitivity. By automatically adjusting authentication requirements based on user behavior or environmental changes, organizations can protect critical data and meet compliance requirements.
See image.

Additionally, administrators can map authentication levels to ACR claims in external identity provider connections to request a particular authentication context. Based on the ACR, the IdP challenges the user with an appropriate authentication policy.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Step-Up Authentication and Configuring Authentication Levels.

entries.title: Support for Revoking Access Tokens
body: You can revoke access tokens assigned to API clients to access the Zscaler service API resources.
See image.
To learn more, see About Access Tokens and Revoking Access Tokens.

entries.title: Changes to Login ID Attribute Mapping
body: The Login ID user attribute is no longer part of the default user attributes and the option to map it for the Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning as an optional configuration has been removed. All external identity providers (IdPs) added to the ZIdentity Admin Portal must mandatorily include mapping for the Login ID attribute with the corresponding SAML or OIDC attribute, depending on the protocol used for the IdP integration. By default, the new IdP integrations map the Login ID attribute with sub or NameID or value for OIDC or SAML-based configurations respectively. You can map other attributes with the Login ID attribute based on your requirements.

The option to map the Login ID attribute has been moved from the Provisioning tab to the Basic tab within the Add Primary Identity Provider window (or Add Secondary Identity Provider window) accessed from Integrations > External Identities.
See image.
If you have enabled JIT provisioning for your external IdPs and mapped the Login ID attribute, the mapping is retained, but the option is moved to the Basic tab.
See image.
To learn more, see About Attributes, About External Identity Providers, Adding OpenID Providers, and Adding SAML Identity Providers.

entries.title: ZIdentity Dashboard
body: The ZIdentity Admin Portal dashboard tracks user activity and provides a high-level overview of all users that are managed from ZIdentity. The dashboard displays the number of users, service entitlement assignments, and graphs for authentication and user management event counts.
See image.
To learn more, see About the Dashboard.

entries.title: ZIdentity UI Enhancement
body: ZIdentity's administrative user interface (UI) is updated to Zscaler's modern UX design system. The menu layout is reorganized to make it easier to access common configurations.
To learn more, see What is ZIdentity?

entries.title: Control Multi-Factor Authentication
body: Admins can disable multi-factor authentication (MFA) for service enrollment for users when required. This option is available only for users that have single sign-on (SSO) enabled.
See image.
Admins can allow users to skip two-factor authentication (2FA) for a short duration and use only their password to log in to the assigned Zscaler service admin portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Authentication Methods.

entries.title: MFA Enrollment for Admins
body: After Zscaler-driven admin migration is completed, all ZIdentity admins are required to enroll for multi-factor authentication (MFA). While configuring the admin profile, admins can initially set the password and choose to enroll for MFA immediately or skip it for a default grace period of 14 days. After the default grace period is completed, admins should enroll for MFA before accessing the subscribed Zscaler service admin portals.
To learn more, see Migrating Zscaler Service Admins to ZIdentity and Configuring Authentication Methods.

entries.title: Support for Zscaler Client Connector Features
body: ZIdentity provides support for the following features on Zscaler Client Connector:
- Device groups and service entitlement
- Machine tunnel support
- Device token-based authentication for Zscaler Client Connector as an identity provider (IdP)
- Zscaler Client Connector dynamic service enrollments
To learn more, see Managing Device Groups, Managing Device Token Authentication, and About Zscaler Client Connector.

entries.title: Additional Permission for Administrative Entitlement
body: While adding an admin role, you can now select the Restricted Full permission for administrative entitlements in the ZIdentity Admin Portal. ZIdentity checks an acting administrator's permissions in target services before allowing them to change the entitlement assignment for those services.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding ZSLogin Admin Roles.

entries.title: Predefined Dynamic Groups
body: Users are added to the following dynamic groups based on user data:
- Dynamic Group Registered Domains: Dynamic group of all users from registered domains.
- Dynamic Group Guest Domains: Dynamic group of all users from guest domains.
- Dynamic Group Administrators: Dynamic group of all users with administrative entitlements.
- Zscaler Global Administrators: Initial user group with global administrative entitlements.
- Zscaler Emergency Access: User group that has Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) emergency access entitlement.
To learn more, see About Groups.

entries.title: Support for Zscaler Identity Proxy for Cloud Apps via ZIdentity
body: Zscaler Identity Proxy for Cloud Apps is supported for ZIdentity-enabled Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) tenants.

A new system-defined session attribute, Is Device Managed, mapped to the appropriate external IdP's claim is passed from the ZIdentity service to the Zscaler Identity Proxy to determine the device management status and apply access policies for the cloud apps.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Session Attributes, Adding SAML IdPs, Adding OpenID Providers, and Configuring the Zscaler Identity Proxy for Cloud Apps.

entries.title: ZIdentity Admin Migration
body: ZIdentity admin migration is effective from June 2024. With ZIdentity migration, administrator data and their roles are migrated from various Zscaler services to ZIdentity, offering a unified identity management and authentication experience. Administrators can authenticate and access all Zscaler service admin portals with a single set of credentials, eliminating the need for multiple login credentials.
To learn more, see Migrating Zscaler Service Admins to ZIdentity.

entries.title: Session Attributes for Users
body: ZIdentity provides support session attributes. ZIdentity records attributes related to the user’s session and makes them available to the Zscaler service, like Zscaler Private Access (ZPA). ZPA can define policies to enforce access based on session context. The ZIdentity admins can add and manage the session attributes.
See image.
To learn more, see About Attributes and Adding Session Attributes.

entries.title: Support for Customizing Logo and Emails
body: ZIdentity provides support for rebranding. You can replace the Zscaler logo with a different logo and add a different email address that is used by the Zscaler service to send emails to your users.
To learn more, see Customizing Branding.

entries.title: Support for Department Attribute
body: Department is available as a system-defined user attribute that can be viewed and edited in the ZIdentity Admin Portal. You can assign users to the required department.
See image.
To learn more, see About Departments and Adding Users.

entries.title: Support for Multi-Factor Authentication
body: You can now enable and enforce multi-factor authentication for users that authenticate to ZSLogin. The users can choose to configure their authentication preferences to access their ZSLogin account based on the authentication methods (Administration > Authentication Methods) set by the ZSLogin admin.
See image.
As a ZSLogin admin, you can view and manage the authenticators for each user from their respective user window (Administration > Users > click the Edit icon for the user > Security Settings).
See image.
To learn more, see Setting Up Your Zscaler Account, Configuring Authentication Methods, Configuring Authentication Preference, and Viewing User Entitlements and Authenticators.

entries.title: Support for OpenID Connect
body: ZSLogin service now supports the OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocol as a Relying Party (RP). OIDC is a single sign-on protocol much like SAML, which is used to authenticate users at your OpenID Provider (OP) and to assert their authenticated identities to ZSLogin.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding OpenID Provider.

entries.title: Support for User Enrollment to Zscaler Services
body: You can now use the ZSLogin service to enroll users to your subscribed Zscaler services, mitigating the effort of managing users for each service separately.
See image.
To support this feature:

- The ZSLogin Admin Portal is introduced with a new Entitlements section inside the Administration menu (Administration > Administrative and Administration > Service) to manage service admins and service users separately.
See image.
- The existing Zscaler Services page (Administration > Zscaler Services) is no longer available.
See image.

- You can configure role-based administration for ZSLogin admins to implement granular permissions, such as controlling whether or not an admin can modify user records, assigning users to services, etc.
See image.
- You can view the service assignments for each user from their respective user window (Administration > Users > click the Edit icon for the user > Entitlements).
See image.

- Two new options, Authentication Session for service enrollment and Force Authentication for Private Access Reauthentication, are added to the Advanced Settings page (Administration > Advanced Settings).
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Entitlements, About ZSLogin Admin Roles, Configuring Advanced Settings and Viewing User Entitlements and Authenticators.
